query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing 50 at.% Pt into FeCoNiMnCu high‐entropy alloy films will increase the coercive field by transforming the high-symmetry fcc phase into a low-symmetry L10 ordered phase that exhibits enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain wall pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiMnCu high‐entropy alloy films deposited in the as-formed state, predominantly exhibiting a cubic fcc structure with moderate coercivity.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by incorporating 50 at.% Pt into FeCoNiMnCu during film deposition.
generation.conditions: Under controlled sputtering deposition followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) to facilitate phase transformation; processing conditions must stabilize the L10 ordering.
generation.structural_mediator: Conversion from a high-symmetry fcc phase to a chemically ordered, low-symmetry tetragonal L10 phase.
generation.mechanism: Pt addition promotes L10 phase formation due to its strong spin‐orbit coupling and its ability to reduce symmetry, thereby enhancing intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy and improving domain wall pinning, which in turn increases the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant increase in the coercive field relative to the baseline FeCoNiMnCu film without Pt addition, while the overall saturation magnetization may be modestly affected.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiMnCu high‐entropy alloy films produced under identical deposition and annealing procedures but without any Pt addition, exhibiting predominantly fcc structure and lower coercivity.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected to hold when the processing conditions (sputtering, RTA) reliably produce a single L10 phase, and may not occur if processing parameters or compositional variations prevent L10 stabilization.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the increase in coercivity is uncertain and will depend on the degree of L10 ordering and the precise processing parameters used.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of high‐entropy alloy films using identical sputtering and RTA conditions: one set with 50 at.% Pt added to the FeCoNiMnCu composition and a control set without Pt. Characterize the crystalline phases using X-ray diffraction (XRD) to verify the formation of the L10 phase in the Pt-added samples. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature for both sets to determine their coercive fields.
measurements: XRD to identify phase structure and confirm L10 ordering
Magnetic hysteresis loop measurements to quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-added films do not exhibit clear formation of a low-symmetry L10 phase and do not show a statistically significant increase in coercivity compared to the Pt-free films, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.
